analysis.evidence: הָעַיִט names the birds of prey as the subject, and עַל הַפְּגָרִים gives their destination, “onto the carcasses.” Abram then drives the birds away.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with the collective singular subject הָעַיִט.

draft.change: Add the masculine noun עַיִט under עיט with its bird-of-prey sense and document its collective use.
draft.definition: A bird of prey that may feed on carrion.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:11 the birds descend on the carcasses and Abram drives them away.

analysis.evidence: The singular verb וַיֵּרֶד agrees with הָעַיִט as the subject descending on the carcasses. When Abram drives the birds away, the plural object אֹתָם refers back to them, showing that the singular noun denotes a group.
analysis.morphology: הָ is the definite article before ע. עַיִט is a masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, used collectively here.
analysis.sense: Bird of prey, here one that feeds on carrion.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּרֶד הָעַיִט עַל הַפְּגָרִים, עַל introduces the carcasses as the place upon which the bird of prey descended.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a root entry for נשב with the Hiphil sense drive-away.
draft.definition: In the Hiphil, to drive away, as Abram drives birds of prey off the carcasses.
draft.evidence: In Gen.15.11 the birds descend on the carcasses, and Abram responds with an action directed at them, וַיַּשֵּׁב אֹתָם.

analysis.evidence: The birds of prey (הָעַיִט, a collective singular) descend on the carcasses. The plural object אֹתָם refers back to the birds as a group. Abram drives them off the carcasses.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with Abram as its subject. The initial נ of the root assimilates to שׁ, accounting for the dagesh in שּׁ.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּשֵּׁב אֹתָם אַבְרָם, Abram is the subject of וַיַּשֵּׁב, “drove away.” The pronoun אֹתָם refers to the birds of prey that descended on the carcasses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham
